records.issue_text: **`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:22-49`** — Authorization bug: for team installs, the function only checks that the requesting user is an *accepted member* of the team (`members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }`) and then creates the credential and `return`s — the `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` check is only reached on the *non-team* branch (where `state?.teamId` is always falsy at that point, since the team branch already returned). Any regular team member — not just team admins/owners — can therefore install/link OAuth app credentials on behalf of the whole team. Given the helper's name and the fact it exists specifically to gate this kind of action, this looks like an inverted/misplaced check rather than intentional design. Fix: call `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId })` inside the `if (state?.teamId)` branch instead of the member-only lookup, and drop the now-dead `state?.teamId ?? null` call after it.

**`refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14`** — the outbound `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no `response.ok` check, no timeout, and sends no authentication/shared secret, asymmetric with the inbound webhook (`app-credential.ts`) which does verify a shared secret. A misbehaving or unreachable sync endpoint will have its (possibly error-page) body treated as a valid token response with no error surfaced beyond a generic parse failure downstream, and there's no way for the receiving endpoint to authenticate that the request truly came from Cal.com.
records.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, it performs a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no `response.ok`/status handling and no timeout/abort, so failures/hangs can propagate unpredictably. records.issue_text: **`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:56-93`** — find-then-create/update instead of an atomic upsert (acknowledged in the code's own comment: "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential"). Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appSlug)` can race and create duplicate credential rows. If the schema has (or can have) a unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`, an upsert keyed on that compound unique would remove the race; otherwise this should at least be documented as a known limitation.
